## Purpose

This SOP describes the determination of soil microbial biomass carbon
(MBC) using the chloroform fumigation-extraction (CFE) method. Chloroform
vapor lyses microbial cells, releasing intracellular carbon that is then
extracted with 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ and quantified as dissolved organic carbon
(DOC) [@vance1987; @joergensen1996].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field-moist soil samples collected per
  [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling and Processing](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)
  for microbial biomass assessment.
- **Does not apply to:** Air-dried or frozen soils (unless pre-validated
  for this method); microbial biomass nitrogen (requires additional
  analytical steps).
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve protocol, ensure safety compliance              |
| Trained Personnel | Perform fumigation and extraction, report results       |
| New Students      | Complete training and safety orientation before use     |


## Definitions

- **Chloroform fumigation-extraction (CFE):** The standard method for
  measuring soil microbial biomass carbon; soil is fumigated with
  ethanol-free chloroform to lyse microbial cells, then extracted with
  K~2~SO~4~; MBC is calculated as the difference in extractable C between
  fumigated and unfumigated soils divided by the $k_{EC}$ factor
  [@vance1987].
- **Extractable organic carbon (EOC):** The organic carbon recovered
  from soil in K~2~SO~4~ extract; includes a background pool of soluble
  organic carbon from non-microbial sources as well as carbon released
  from lysed microbial cells.
- **$k_{EC}$ factor:** The extraction efficiency correction factor for
  microbial biomass carbon; commonly 0.45, meaning 45% of lysed microbial
  carbon is recovered in the extract; must be stated when reporting results
  [@vance1987; @joergensen1996].
- **Microbial biomass carbon (MBC):** The total carbon contained in the
  living soil microbial community (bacteria, fungi, protozoa, nematodes);
  expressed as mg C kg^-1^ oven-dry soil; a key indicator of soil
  biological health and nutrient cycling potential [@robertson1999].
- **Potentially mineralizable nitrogen (PMN):** The nitrogen that can be
  released from soil organic matter by microbial activity under aerobic
  conditions; correlated with microbial biomass and organic matter quality.
- **Unfumigated control:** Soil extracted with K~2~SO~4~ without prior
  chloroform fumigation; provides the background extractable carbon value
  subtracted from the fumigated extract to calculate MBC [@vance1987].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Warning

Chloroform (CHCl~3~) is a volatile, toxic solvent and a suspected
carcinogen. All fumigation steps must be performed inside a fume hood.
Do not inhale chloroform vapors. Use ethanol-free chloroform only
[@fao2024].
:::

### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Chloroform (toxic, volatile, suspected carcinogen); 0.5 M
  K~2~SO~4~ (mild irritant).
- **Physical:** Vacuum desiccator under reduced pressure; risk of
  implosion if cracked.

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (double-gloving recommended when handling chloroform)
- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Laboratory coat
- [ ] Work inside a fume hood at all times during fumigation

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chloroform spill, refer to the SDS and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
Evacuate the area if the spill is large; ventilate the space and notify
the supervisor.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Vacuum desiccator             | Glass, with stopcock and vacuum line         |
| Vacuum pump                   | Oil-free preferred                           |
| Fume hood                     | Required for all chloroform handling         |
| Orbital or end-over-end shaker | For extraction step                         |
| Centrifuge                    | Capable of 4,000 × g (optional)              |
| Filtration apparatus          | With 0.45 µm glass fiber filters             |
| Analytical balance            | 0.01 g resolution                            |
| Incubator or dark cabinet     | For 24-hour fumigation at room temperature   |
| TOC analyzer                  | Shimadzu TOC-L; see [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd) |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Ethanol-free chloroform       | ACS grade; stored in fume hood               |
| 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ solution     | Prepare fresh or within 1 week               |
| Glass fiber filters (0.45 µm) | Pre-combusted at 450 °C for 4 hours          |
| Boiling chips or glass beads  | For chloroform evaporation under vacuum      |
| Extraction bottles (100 mL)   | Screw-top, HDPE or glass                     |
| Filter funnels and flasks     | Clean, acid-washed                           |
| Sample vials                  | Acid-washed, for filtered extracts           |


## Procedure

### Preparation

1. Prepare 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ by dissolving 87.1 g K~2~SO~4~ per liter of
   deionized water. The 1:4 soil-to-extractant ratio is standard for
   CFE [@vance1987].
2. Pre-combust glass fiber filters at 450 °C for 4 hours and store in a
   clean container.
3. Determine the gravimetric moisture content of a separate subsample
   (dry at 105 °C for 24 hours per
   [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)) so results can be expressed
   on an oven-dry-weight basis.

### Fumigation

1. Weigh two paired subsamples of 15 g field-moist soil into labeled
   extraction bottles.
2. Place one set (fumigated) into the vacuum desiccator inside the fume
   hood.
3. Place a beaker containing approximately 30 mL of ethanol-free
   chloroform and a few boiling chips in the center of the desiccator.
4. Evacuate the desiccator using the vacuum pump until the chloroform
   begins to boil vigorously (approximately 2 minutes) [@vance1987].
5. Close the stopcock and incubate in the dark at room temperature
   (approximately 25 °C) for 24 hours [@vance1987; @fao2024].
6. The second set (unfumigated controls) is extracted immediately
   (proceed to §6.3).

### Extraction

1. After 24 hours, release the vacuum inside the fume hood and remove
   the chloroform beaker.
2. Evacuate the desiccator repeatedly (3--5 times) to remove residual
   chloroform vapor from the soil.
3. Add 60 mL of 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ to each bottle (both fumigated and
   unfumigated), achieving a 1:4 soil-to-extractant ratio [@vance1987].
4. Cap bottles and shake on an orbital or end-over-end shaker for 1 hour.
5. Allow the suspension to settle briefly, or centrifuge at 4,000 × g
   for 10 minutes.
6. Filter the supernatant through a pre-combusted 0.45 µm glass fiber
   filter into a clean sample vial.
7. Store filtered extracts at 4 °C if not analyzed immediately; analyze
   within 48 hours.

### DOC Analysis

1. Analyze filtered extracts for dissolved organic carbon using the
   Shimadzu TOC-L per [SOP-L407 Total Carbon](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd).
2. Run 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ blanks alongside samples.

### Calculation

Microbial biomass carbon is calculated as [@vance1987; @joergensen1996]:

$$
\text{MBC} = \frac{C_{\text{fumigated}} - C_{\text{unfumigated}}}{k_{EC}}
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{fumigated}}$ = DOC in the fumigated extract (mg C kg^-1^
  oven-dry soil)
- $C_{\text{unfumigated}}$ = DOC in the unfumigated extract (mg C kg^-1^
  oven-dry soil)
- $k_{EC}$ = 0.45, the extraction efficiency coefficient [@vance1987;
  @joergensen1996]

::: {.callout-note}
The unfumigated extract DOC value represents the background dissolved
organic carbon pool and is often reported separately as an indicator of
labile soil carbon [@robertson1999].
:::


## Quality Control

- Run analytical triplicates for at least 10% of samples; the
  coefficient of variation among replicates should be less than 15%
  [@fao2024].
- Include a reagent blank (0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ only, no soil) in each batch.
- Include a laboratory reference soil in each batch to monitor method
  consistency.
- Verify that the TOC calibration $r^2 \geq 0.999$ before reporting
  results.

| Used soil                    | Solid waste bag        | Standard trash                |
| Used glass fiber filters     | Standard trash         | Standard trash                |

## Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the SDS for chloroform
3. Observe a trained operator perform the full fumigation-extraction
   procedure
4. Demonstrate competence with vacuum desiccator operation
5. Perform the procedure under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
